message.content:
The number of distinct legal positions that can arise in a game of chess is astronomically large.  In fact, the best estimates put it at roughly

\[
10^{43}\text{–}10^{50}
\]

different arrangements of pieces on the board.  

A commonly cited figure is the **Shannon number**, named after Claude Shannon, which is about \(10^{43}\).  More recent analyses that take into account all the rules of chess (castling rights, en‑passant, pawn promotion, etc.) suggest a slightly higher bound, on the order of \(10^{46}\) to \(10^{48}\).

So, while the exact count is still a subject of research, the consensus is that there are on the order of **tens of trillions of trillions of trillions** of possible legal chess positions.
